entries.name: Where Life & Scripture Meet (CCEF)
entries.creator: Alasdair Groves (former host) and CCEF faculty
subject: Biblical Counseling
Mental Health
Christian Living
entries.doctrinal_basis: CCEF describes its approach as gospel-based ministry to struggling Christians. Its statement of faith was not checked this session; read it on CCEF’s site.
points_to_weigh: Biblical counseling is not a substitute for medical or clinical care. If you or someone you know struggles with OCD, consider seeing a licensed clinician as well as a pastor or counselor.
Sources differ on how far clinical therapy and pastoral counseling should be combined (see the other counseling podcasts in this list).
notable_episodes: OCD with Mike Emlet, Part 2 (13 June 2017): a gospel-based ministry approach to Christians troubled by obsessive doubt, scrupulosity and an overly sensitive conscience. https://www.ccef.org/podcast/ocd-mike-emlet-part-2/
entries.description: The podcast of the Christian Counseling & Educational Foundation (CCEF), on biblical counseling for anxiety, depression, OCD and other struggles.

entries.name: Christian Faith and OCD, Scrupulosity, Intrusive Thoughts, Compulsions
entries.creator: Carrie Bock, Licensed Professional Counselor
subject: Mental Health
Christian Living
entries.doctrinal_basis: Explicitly Christian; no denomination or confession is stated.
points_to_weigh: Not a Reformed ministry. The host is a licensed counselor and teaches a clinical approach (ICBT); it is included because it deals directly with religious OCD.

The host argues that church culture and biblical counseling can unintentionally reinforce the OCD cycle. Biblical-counseling ministries (CCEF and ACBC above) take a different approach, so weigh them together with your pastor and a licensed clinician.
This is not medical advice.
entries.description: Podcast about living with OCD and scrupulosity from a Christian perspective, teaching an inference-based cognitive behavioral approach (ICBT); more than 240 episodes.
